I don't trust the Play Store with installs and the binaries it produces. When Google updates and restarts your phone, it "optimizes" all your apps, whether they came from the Play Store or not.

Android apps are made with Java, which is an interpreted language. Interpreted languages are tremendously slow compared to compiled languages.

When you run an Android device for the first time, or upgrade the Android version, for every app, parts of code are collected into an "odex" file, so that particular app will boot faster. This is what the "optimizing" actually is.

This process is also why Android apps are tremendously easy to hack. An apk file is literally zipped source code. The furthest away you can get from that is the addition of an "obb" or Oblique Binary Blob, which is a precompiled resource file. That's what "additional files" are. You still need the apk to run it though.
